name: AVERAGEIF
description: AVERAGEIF calculates the average of cells that meet a single criterion.
tldr: Averages values that satisfy one condition.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: The range to evaluate against the criteria.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The condition that determines which cells to average.

parameters.name: average_range
parameters.description: The actual cells to average. If omitted, range is used.

basicExample.description: Average score for a specific class
basicExample.explanation: Averages values in B2:B100 only where A2:A100 is "Class A".

advancedExamples.title: Average above a threshold
advancedExamples.explanation: Only values above 1000 are included in the average.

howItWorks: AVERAGEIF evaluates the criteria against each cell in range. For matching cells, it averages the corresponding value from average_range (or range itself if average_range is omitted).
limitations: Criteria ranges must match average_range in size.
Empty cells in average_range are ignored.

commonErrors.fix: Check that the criteria is correct and that matching values exist.

commonErrors.cause: Text values in average_range are ignored.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: AVERAGEIF works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between AVERAGEIF and AVERAGEIFS?
faq.answer: AVERAGEIF handles one criterion. AVERAGEIFS handles multiple criteria.
